title: The Planet Where It Rains GLASS Sideways ☔
description:
There's a planet where it rains glass, sideways: HD 189733b, a gas giant 64 light-years away. It hugs its star (about 13 times closer than Mercury is to our Sun, so a year there lasts about two days), and its sky is around 1,000 °C. That's hot enough that rock goes up as vapour and comes back down as tiny bits of glass: scientists think its clouds are made of silica, the stuff of sand and glass, and in 2024 the Webb telescope picked up their signal. Then winds measured at over 8,700 km/h (faster than a bullet) blow the glass sideways. All that glass may be why the planet looks deep blue. And Webb also found hydrogen sulfide in its air: the gas that makes rotten eggs stink. Umbrella or helmet?

Subscribe for a new strange question every day.
